create.name: Tushita Mahayana Meditation Centre, Delhi
create.bio:
Tushita Mahayana Meditation Centre is a Tibetan Buddhist centre in Hauz Khas, New Delhi, set up in 1979 with the guidance of Lama Thubten Yeshe and Lama Zopa Rinpoche, who founded the FPMT. It belongs to that worldwide network of Gelug Buddhist centres and looks to the Dalai Lama as one of its spiritual guides. Its director is the sociologist and author Professor Renuka Singh, who has been connected with the centre since the early 1980s.

The centre runs drop-in meditation and contemplation sessions in its hall and on Zoom, where a visiting teacher or an experienced student leads a short practice, a talk on a set theme and time for questions. Short guided meditations are held online on weekday mornings, mixing mindfulness with the analytical style of Tibetan practice, and there are weekly pujas and group recitation of the Sanghata Sutra. Everything is offered on a donation basis, with no need to register. Its YouTube channel, started in 2015, keeps full recordings of talks by geshes, nuns and lay teachers on lamrim, emptiness, karma and compassion, along with guided analytical meditations.

free_resources.title: Meditation and Contemplation Drop-in Sessions
free_resources.description: Ninety-minute sessions at the centre and on Zoom, each with a short meditation, a talk on the day's theme and questions. No registration; a donation box is at the back of the hall.

free_resources.title: Morning Guided Meditation
free_resources.description: Thirty-minute online meditations on weekday mornings (India time), alternating mindfulness and analytical practice. Free and open to all.

free_resources.title: Sanghata Sutra Recitation
free_resources.description: Group recitation of the Sanghata Sutra, a practice Lama Zopa Rinpoche asked FPMT centres to keep up.
